items.title: 63519_Wild Bill Davison oral history interview
items.q: I had a friend of mine who had then managing a big band on the road and his name was Carl Dunbar

ctx.x: No - no -- and, so, he booked me in that and while we're unloading the band out there in front of the Savoy -- an all colored ballroom -- and we're playing that night against Tiny Parham, and I just happened to look up at the canopy and it said ---"Wild Bill Davison - the White Louis Armstrong." Well, I almost fainted. I was ready to jump in the car and go back - the north side of Chicago - that scared the hell out of me. But, we went in and we did a job and we got--- really got more applause in an all colored…

wasn't the same. Wasn't the same band he hired---so, it only lasted a couple of weeks and that was it. And, so, at that point, I had a friend of mine who had then managing a big band on the road and his name was Carl Dunbar, and Carl was around Chicago in those days and he came up to this little place where I was staying and he said -- listen, I've been offered the managementship of the Wisconsin Ballroom in Milwaukee-- he said, how would you like to come to Milwaukee and you got the band-- we'll get on the…
That was up on that -- the Wisconsin River.
